findings.summary: The 'crates.io' destination word can never match the tokenizer's alphanumeric words, so the planned positive case 'Publish the crate to crates.io' fails as written.
findings.evidence: Step 2 splits words on any character that is not alphanumeric or an apostrophe, so 'crates.io' becomes the two tokens 'crates' and 'io'. The destination entry 'crates.io' can then never equal a token. 'crate' and 'crates' are both PACKAGE_NOUNS, which need a destination or version token, so 'Publish the crate to crates.io' is not detected and the positive assertion in delivery_verbs_are_found_after_lead_ins_and_markers fails. The segment rule keeps the dot inside one segment, but that does not join the tokens. Fix: Match destination words with has_phrase on the window's text span (from the verb to the end of the window), not by token equality. Alternatively, have the tokenizer keep '.' inside a word when letters follow it. Keep the 'crates.io' positive case in the test either way.
findings.location: Plan step 2 (tokenizer: words are runs of alphanumeric characters) vs. step 1 DESTINATION_WORDS ('crates.io') and the criterion 3 demonstration ('Publish the crate to crates.io' must be detected)

findings.summary: The error offers 'Publishing is out of scope' as an equal repair, which invites the reader to repair the g6vy misread by narrowing it explicitly.
findings.evidence: Read the reader way, g6vy was a request to publish that was narrowed to a file. The reader gets one re-read with the refusal text (Athena::read_for). If the error offers the out_of_scope line as an equal repair, the cheapest fix for the same misread is to add 'Publishing is out of scope'. The narrowing is then visible to the user, but it is still the misread. Fix: Order the repairs in the error. Name a behavior criterion with a reachable URL, a served page or a downloadable release first. Offer the out_of_scope line only for the case where the request does not ask for the delivery itself, for example: 'only if the request does not ask you to publish'. Record this in D161.
findings.location: Plan step 3 (error text gives 'Publishing is out of scope' as a repair) and decision 6

findings.summary: The 'not the other two' half of the criterion 2 replay uses stand-in text and cannot fail. The plan says so, but the open question must be settled before production.
findings.evidence: The recorded request texts of 7bf8 and 0wtc are not in the snapshot. A Grep finds only the paraphrases in decisions.md D94 (line 2105) and D152 (line 4113), so the 'not the other two' half runs on text the planner wrote. The plan labels it as not a measurement and asks the host and the user. Still, criterion 2 as accepted says 'recorded request text of all three', and that half cannot fail. Fix: Keep the labelling. Have the open question to the host and the user settled before the producer runs. If the texts are supplied, write them verbatim and set verbatim to true. If not, make the CHANGELOG and D161 say plainly that only g6vy was replayed. The plan already makes the CHANGELOG assertion require 'not replayed' while any entry is a stand-in.

findings.summary: 'pages' is in two word lists, and the second entry does nothing.
findings.evidence: 'pages' is in both VISIBLE_NOUNS and DESTINATION_WORDS. Because the window accepts either list, the duplicate entry does nothing. Fix: Keep 'pages' in one list, or add a comment on why it is in both.

summary: I read reading.rs (refusing_check 3225-3250, check_governance_coverage 3291-3363, has_phrase 3399, producer_evidence_phrase and check_criteria_evidence 3409-3474, the governance tests 7013-7257, the replay limits 3736/3884/4027), refusal_corpus.rs (base_reading class docs, INPUT_FORMS of 17, run(), function_body, the anchor at line 801, the CHANGELOG assertion at 859, the brand-word case at 559), the READING_RULES test in briefs.rs, the decisions-log pin test and backtest PHRASES, and docs/decision-links.toml. The functions, line numbers and seams the plan names exist as described. check_outcome_state and refusing_check are reached only from athena-core: reading.rs and refusal_corpus.rs. Every delivery-verb string literal in reading.rs tests is on the plan's dependents list: NAMED_PATH_REQUESTS, COMMON_WORD_REQUESTS, the workflow test, the retry test and the declined/asking/empty test. The only corpus case with a delivery verb is brand-word. No criterion the new tests add contains a producer-evidence phrase. D161 can be appended after D160, which is the last entry, without touching the pinned prefix. reading.rs is not a governed path. The demonstrations call real entry points with plain Reading fixtures and would fail without the check. On soundness, the approach is still a word-table heuristic, but it is bounded: verb position, an object window, noun-use and technical-noun rules, the requirement that a state phrase appear in a behavior criterion, and a one-line repair. It cites the precedent of the removed governance word table and states its known false refusal ('Release the page lock'). Given the scope the user accepted, I do not find it crude. I found three minor issues. A tokenizer inconsistency would make one planned assertion fail as written. The out_of_scope repair could steer the single re-read back to the narrowed reading. The stand-in half of the criterion 2 replay cannot fail, and the plan already says so. None of the three blocks the plan.
